brief: Since #24 the diorama answers a click on 64% of the frame and the cursor changes to say so — but nothing says WHAT you are pointing at. The courtyard beds hold eleven species with bloom stages, there are thirteen trees each on their own seasonal clock, and a viewer cannot name a single one. Give the picture a quiet identification of the thing under the pointer: this bed is lavender coming into bloom, this is the linden in leaf-turn, this is a cabbage plot standing through the cold. Read what the cell actually holds off the grid; do not guess from position. Why now: the courtyard has had no iteration since #14, eleven back and the most starved domain in the town, and it is where the nameable content is densest.
successLooksLike: Ten seconds of moving the pointer over the courtyard teaches a viewer three plant names they did not arrive with, and the naming stays correct as the season changes what is actually growing there.
avoid: No permanent labels painted on the canvas. Do not fire on every mousemove — a name that changes sixty times a second is noise, not information. Do not fight the one-time invitation (inviteHold owns the sill while it runs). And mobile has no cursor at all, so a hover-only affordance is a discovery rate of zero on a tracked framing — see how the invitation borrows the sill at 390px.
